answer: An attacker renting cloud servers hits a hardware wall. Each key is bound to a prism, the vendor-signed attestation quote of one physical enclave chip, and the ledger rejects any second key whose prism names a chip already registered. Votes are signed by a cipher, a session key sealed inside that enclave, so no vote can be forged off the chip. A key whose chip fails the weekly re-attestation falls to nadir, a state with zero vote weight. Fielding 200 clones means buying and powering 200 separate chips, roughly 60,000 dollars, while an honest agent needs one.
